```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# VIGAT calls the OpenAI API and reads fragment files, so the analysis code
# below is shown but not run when the vignette is built. Tables and figures
# come from a precomputed run on the same data (files in data/ and figures/).
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      comment = "#>")
```

## Overview

Gene activity scores for single-cell ATAC-seq are usually computed by counting
fragments over a fixed region for every gene, such as the gene body plus 2 kb
upstream. A fixed rule can miss where the informative accessibility actually is:
the cell-type-specific signal may sit in a short promoter peak, be offset from
the annotated TSS, or be mixed with signal from a neighbouring gene.

**VIGAT** (VLM-guided gene activity quantification) chooses the region gene by
gene, the way an analyst would by eye. For each marker gene it

1. draws a coverage plot of the ±5 kb around the TSS, with one track per ATAC
   cluster, the gene model and the called peaks;
2. sends the plots to a vision-language model (VLM) with instructions to pick
   one compact window that captures the clearest cluster-specific promoter signal;
3. counts fragments in the selected windows to build a gene-by-cell matrix.

All of this happens in a single call to `VIGAT()`.

This vignette runs VIGAT on a human pancreatic islet sample with 15 marker genes
for 7 cell types.

## Installation

```{r}
install.packages(c("Seurat", "Signac", "remotes"))
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(c("GenomicRanges", "GenomeInfoDb", "IRanges",
                       "S4Vectors", "BiocGenerics"))
remotes::install_github("beijie02/VIGAT")
```

VIGAT reads your OpenAI API key from the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable.
Add it once to `~/.Renviron`:

```
OPENAI_API_KEY=your_openai_api_key
```

then restart R. Do not put the key in scripts or commit it to GitHub.

```{r}
library(VIGAT)
library(Seurat)
library(Signac)
```

## Example data

The example is the human islet sample GSM7618328_GSM7618327 from
CompassDB. The object has been quality-controlled and clustered on the ATAC data, and the cluster labels are stored in the metadata column `ATAC_cluster`.

Three files are needed: the object `islet_example_atac.rds` (about 3.9 GB), the
fragment file `islet_fragments.tsv.gz` (about 3 GB) and its index
`islet_fragments.tsv.gz.tbi`. Download them into the same folder:

```{r}
options(timeout = 3600)   # large files: allow up to an hour per download
base <- "https://duke.box.com/shared/static"

download.file(file.path(base, "g31hskzlm8865ojydlyjtkurwz3ao4gc.rds"),
              "islet_example_atac.rds", mode = "wb")
download.file(file.path(base, "637jcsxkkw4dxn8oka7k6kig6uo5d905.gz"),
              "islet_fragments.tsv.gz", mode = "wb")
download.file(file.path(base, "7mzirxtynqummqoflwpquq2n9r28cda7.tbi"),
              "islet_fragments.tsv.gz.tbi", mode = "wb")
```

A Signac object stores the location of its fragment file, so point the object
to the downloaded file:

```{r}
obj <- readRDS("islet_example_atac.rds")

frags <- Fragments(obj)
frags[[1]] <- UpdatePath(frags[[1]], new.path = "islet_fragments.tsv.gz")
Fragments(obj) <- NULL
Fragments(obj) <- frags

table(obj$ATAC_cluster)
```

The object has 10,093 cells in 8 ATAC clusters. To make the results easier to
read, the table below labels each cluster with the RNA cell type that most of
its cells belong to. VIGAT does not use these labels; the model only sees the
cluster numbers.

```{r clusters, eval = TRUE, echo = FALSE}
cl <- read.csv("data/islet_atac_cluster_labels.csv")
knitr::kable(cl[, c("ATAC_cluster", "n_cells", "voted_cell_type")],
             col.names = c("ATAC cluster", "Cells", "Majority RNA cell type"),
             align = "lrl", format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## Marker genes

For each cell type present in the sample we use two or three marker genes,
taken from the cell type markers in
[DISCO](https://www.immunesinglecell.com/cell_type).

```{r markers, eval = TRUE, echo = FALSE}
mk <- read.csv("data/islet_marker_genes.csv")
mk_tab <- aggregate(gene ~ target_celltype, data = mk, FUN = paste, collapse = ", ")
knitr::kable(mk_tab, col.names = c("Cell type", "Marker genes"))
```

```{r}
marker_genes <- c("CPA1", "CTRB1", "PRSS1",      # acinar
                  "GCG", "TTR",                 # alpha
                  "IAPP", "INS",                # beta
                  "RBP4", "SST",                # delta
                  "PECAM1", "RAMP2",            # endothelial
                  "DCN", "LUM",                 # fibroblast
                  "SERPINA1", "SPP1")           # ductal
```

## Run VIGAT

One call does the whole analysis:

```{r}
res <- VIGAT(
  obj         = obj,
  genes       = marker_genes,
  tissue      = "Islet",
  species     = "human",
  cluster_col = "ATAC_cluster",
  return_highlighted_plots = TRUE
)
```

Inside `VIGAT()`:

- Cells with no cluster label are removed, and so are clusters with fewer than
  `min_atac_cluster_cells` cells (50 by default). Here every cluster has at
  least 50 cells, so all 10,093 cells are kept.
- For each gene, the TSS and strand are taken from the gene annotation of the
  ATAC assay, and the called peaks within ±5 kb are collected.
- The coverage plots are laid out four genes per page and uploaded to the
  model as PDFs, together with a prompt that lists each gene, its strand and
  the overlapping peaks. The PDFs are written to a temporary folder and
  deleted when `VIGAT()` returns.
- The model returns one window per gene. VIGAT parses the windows and counts
  fragments in them with `Signac::FeatureMatrix()`.

`VIGAT()` writes nothing to disk; everything comes back in `res`. The main
outputs are `res$vigat_windows`, the selected window for each gene, and
`res$count_matrix`, the gene-by-cell matrix of fragment counts in those windows.

```{r run-info, eval = TRUE, echo = FALSE}
ri <- read.csv("data/islet_api_run_info.csv")
```

In this run the model (`r ri$model`) used `r format(ri$total_tokens, big.mark = ",")`
tokens and took about `r round(ri$elapsed_seconds / 60, 1)` minutes for
`r ri$n_genes_found` genes, sent as `r ri$n_pdf_files` PDF pages.

## Selected windows

`res$vigat_windows` is a `GRanges` object with one window per gene, and
`res$vigat_window_df` holds the same information as a data frame. The model also
explains each choice; its reply is kept in `res$diagnostics$raw_response`. The
table below combines the two.

<div style="overflow-x: auto; font-size: 0.85em;">

```{r windows, eval = TRUE, echo = FALSE}
win <- read.csv("data/islet_vigat_windows.csv")
raw <- readLines("data/islet_raw_api_response.txt")
rows <- grep("^[A-Za-z0-9]+; [+-]; chr", raw, value = TRUE)
parts <- strsplit(rows, "; ", fixed = TRUE)
expl <- data.frame(
  gene      = vapply(parts, `[`, "", 1),
  strand    = vapply(parts, `[`, "", 2),
  evidence  = vapply(parts, `[`, "", 5),
  clusters  = vapply(parts, `[`, "", 6),
  rationale = vapply(parts, function(x) paste(x[-(1:6)], collapse = "; "), "")
)
tab <- merge(win, expl, by = "gene", sort = FALSE)
tab <- tab[match(win$gene, tab$gene), ]
tab$strand <- ifelse(tab$strand == "+", "&#43;", "&#8722;")  # HTML entities, so "+"/"-" are not read as list bullets
tab$window <- sprintf("%s:%s-%s", tab$chr,
                      format(tab$start, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE),
                      format(tab$end, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE))
knitr::kable(
  tab[, c("gene", "strand", "window", "width", "evidence", "clusters", "rationale")],
  col.names = c("Gene", "Strand", "Window", "Width (bp)", "Anchor evidence",
                "Strongest clusters", "Model rationale"),
  row.names = FALSE,
  format = "html",
  escape = FALSE,
  table.attr = 'class="table" style="min-width: 1100px;"'
)
```

</div>

All 15 genes received a window between 1.0 and 1.9 kb. Fourteen are anchored on
a called peak; for DCN no peak overlaps the informative signal, so the window
follows the coverage alone.

The strongest clusters named by the model agree with the cell-type labels above
without the model having seen them: acinar genes (CPA1, CTRB1, PRSS1) point to
cluster 7, INS to cluster 0 (beta), PECAM1 and RAMP2 to cluster 5
(endothelial), and DCN to cluster 4 (fibroblast).

## Save the results

Because `VIGAT()` does not write files, save what you need yourself:

```{r}
saveRDS(res, "vigat_islet_result.rds")
write.csv(res$vigat_window_df, "vigat_windows.csv", row.names = FALSE)

for (g in names(res$highlighted_plots)) {
  ggplot2::ggsave(paste0(g, "_vigat.png"), res$highlighted_plots[[g]],
                  width = 11, height = 11, dpi = 150)
}
```

Model replies can differ slightly between runs, so keep the saved result
(including `res$vigat_windows`) for the analysis you report.

## Inspect intermediate results

Set `return_intermediates = TRUE` to also get the inputs VIGAT built for the
model:

```{r}
res <- VIGAT(obj, genes = marker_genes, tissue = "Islet",
             cluster_col = "ATAC_cluster", return_intermediates = TRUE)

res$intermediates$tss_info           # TSS, strand and plotted region per gene
res$intermediates$overlapping_peaks  # called peaks inside each region
res$intermediates$coverage_plots     # the plots sent to the model
cat(res$intermediates$prompt)        # the full prompt
res$intermediates$api_run_info       # model, tokens, time
```

## Options

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `obj` | (required) | Signac Seurat object with an `ATAC` assay, gene annotation and fragment files |
| `genes` | (required) | Marker genes to score |
| `tissue` | (required) | Tissue name given to the model as context, e.g. `"Islet"` |
| `species` | `"human"` | Species given to the model; `NULL` omits it |
| `cluster_col` | `NULL` | Metadata column with ATAC clusters; `NULL` uses `Idents(obj)` |
| `min_atac_cluster_cells` | `50` | Clusters with fewer cells are removed before plotting |
| `openai_model` | `"gpt-5.5"` | OpenAI model that reads the plots |
| `return_intermediates` | `FALSE` | Also return TSS info, peaks, input coverage plots, prompt and API logs |
| `return_highlighted_plots` | `FALSE` | Also return one coverage plot per gene with the selected window highlighted |
